verses.1: These are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each one with his household:
verses.5: In total, the number of souls in Jacob’s lineage was seventy, including Joseph who was already in Egypt.
verses.6: Then Joseph died, along with all his brothers and that entire generation.
verses.7: The children of Israel multiplied and thrived, increasing greatly in number until the land was filled with them.
verses.8: A new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
verses.9: He said to his people, “Look, the people of Israel are too numerous and powerful for us.
verses.10: Come, let us be wise with them, in case they multiply further and in war they join our enemies and rise up against us, taking over the land.”
verses.11: So he set taskmasters over them to afflict them with hard labor. He built store-cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.
verses.12: Yet the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread, to the dismay of the Egyptians.
verses.13: The Egyptians then made the Israelites work brutally.
verses.14: They embittered their lives with harsh labor, with mortar and bricks, and every kind of work in the fields, all the labor imposed on them with cruelty.
verses.15: Then Pharaoh spoke to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah.
verses.16: He said, “When you assist the Hebrew women in childbirth, and you see them on the birthstool, if it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live.”
verses.17: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded. They let the children live.
verses.18: So Pharaoh called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, letting the children live?”
verses.19: The midwives replied to Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they give birth before the midwife arrives.”
verses.20: And God was kind to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
verses.21: Because the midwives feared God, He gave them houses.
verses.22: Then Pharaoh gave orders to all his people, saying, “Every newborn Hebrew boy you must cast into the river, but every girl you may let live.”

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "the children of Israel" is a standard rendering for בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, which can also be "the Israelites."  
- v. 15: Midwives are commonly referred to as such in modern English, rather than "those who assisted in birth" or "those who delivered."  
- v. 22: "the river" refers to the Nile; the Hebrew does not name the river, but the context makes it clear.
raw:
[1] These are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each one with his household:  
[2] Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah.  
[3] Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin.  
[4] Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.  
[5] In total, the number of souls in Jacob’s lineage was seventy, including Joseph who was already in Egypt.  
[6] Then Joseph died, along with all his brothers and that entire generation.  
[7] The children of Israel multiplied and thrived, increasing greatly in number until the land was filled with them.  
[8] A new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.  
[9] He said to his people, “Look, the people of Israel are too numerous and powerful for us.  
[10] Come, let us be wise with them, in case they multiply further and in war they join our enemies and rise up against us, taking over the land.”  
[11] So he set taskmasters over them to afflict them with hard labor. He built store-cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.  
[12] Yet the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread, to the dismay of the Egyptians.  
[13] The Egyptians then made the Israelites work brutally.  
[14] They embittered their lives with harsh labor, with mortar and bricks, and every kind of work in the fields, all the labor imposed on them with cruelty.  
[15] Then Pharaoh spoke to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah.  
[16] He said, “When you assist the Hebrew women in childbirth, and you see them on the birthstool, if it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live.”  
[17] The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded. They let the children live.  
[18] So Pharaoh called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, letting the children live?”  
[19] The midwives replied to Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they give birth before the midwife arrives.”  
[20] And God was kind to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.  
[21] Because the midwives feared God, He gave them houses.  
[22] Then Pharaoh gave orders to all his people, saying, “Every newborn Hebrew boy you must cast into the river, but every girl you may let live.”  

---  
Notes  
- v. 1: "the children of Israel" is a standard rendering for בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, which can also be "the Israelites."  
- v. 15: Midwives are commonly referred to as such in modern English, rather than "those who assisted in birth" or "those who delivered."  
- v. 22: "the river" refers to the Nile; the Hebrew does not name the river, but the context makes it clear.
